title: एकोनाशीतितमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 79 · The brothers long for Arjuna

summary.en: In the Kamyaka forest the Pandavas and Draupadi pine for Arjuna, recalling his prowess. Nakula and Sahadeva and Draupadi say the forest has lost its charm without him, and they resolve to move on.
summary.kn: ಕಾಮ್ಯಕವನದಲ್ಲಿ ಪಾಂಡವರು ದ್ರೌಪದಿ ಅರ್ಜುನನ ಪರಾಕ್ರಮವನ್ನು ನೆನೆದು ಹಂಬಲಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ. ಅವನಿಲ್ಲದೆ ಕಾಡು ಸೊಬಗು ಕಳೆದುಕೊಂಡಿದೆ ಎಂದು ನಕುಲ, ಸಹದೇವ, ದ್ರೌಪದಿ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾರೆ; ಅವರು ಮುಂದೆ ಸಾಗಲು ನಿಶ್ಚಯಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ.
summary.hi: काम्यक वन में पाण्डव और द्रौपदी अर्जुन के पराक्रम को याद कर उनके लिए तरसते हैं। नकुल, सहदेव और द्रौपदी कहते हैं कि उनके बिना वन की शोभा चली गई है, और वे आगे बढ़ने का निश्चय करते हैं।
summary.te: కామ్యకవనంలో పాండవులు, ద్రౌపది అర్జునుని పరాక్రమాన్ని తలచుకొని తపిస్తారు. అతడు లేకుండా అడవి అందం కోల్పోయిందని నకులుడు, సహదేవుడు, ద్రౌపది అంటారు; వారు ముందుకు సాగాలని నిశ్చయిస్తారు.
summary.ta: காம்யக வனத்தில் பாண்டவர்களும் திரௌபதியும் அர்ஜுனனின் வீரத்தை நினைத்து ஏங்குகிறார்கள். அவன் இல்லாமல் காடு அழகை இழந்துவிட்டது என்று நகுலன், ஸஹதேவன், திரௌபதி சொல்ல, அவர்கள் மேலே செல்லத் தீர்மானிக்கிறார்கள்.
summary.ml: കാമ്യകവനത്തിൽ പാണ്ഡവരും ദ്രൗപദിയും അർജുനന്റെ പരാക്രമങ്ങൾ ഓർത്ത് അദ്ദേഹത്തെ കാണാതെ വിഷമിക്കുന്നു. നകുലനും സഹദേവനും ദ്രൗപദിയും പറയുന്നു, അദ്ദേഹമില്ലാതെ വനത്തിന് മനോഹാരിത നഷ്ടപ്പെട്ടു; അവർ അവിടം വിട്ടുപോകാൻ തീരുമാനിക്കുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 3.79; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Apr 11 2022

verses.text: जनमेजय उवाच

meaning.en: Janamejaya said:

verses.text:
भगवन्काम्यकात्पार्थे गते मे प्रपितामहे ।
पाण्डवाः किमकुर्वन्त तमृते सव्यसाचिनम् ॥

meaning.en: Blessed sir, after Partha, my great-grandfather, left Kamyaka, what did the Pandavas do without Savyasachi?

verses.text:
स हि तेषां महेष्वासो गतिरासीदनीकजित् ।
आदित्यानां यथा विष्णुस्तथैव प्रतिभाति मे ॥

meaning.en: That great archer, conqueror of armies, was their refuge. To me he seems among them as Vishnu is among the Adityas.

verses.text:
तेनेन्द्रसमवीर्येण संग्रामेष्वनिवर्तिना ।
विनाभूता वने वीराः कथमासन्पितामहाः ॥

meaning.en: How did my grandfathers, those heroes, live in the forest without him, a man of Indra's strength who never turned back in battle?

verses.text: वैशंपायन उवाच

meaning.en: Vaishampayana said:

verses.text:
गते तु काम्यकात्तात पाण्डवे सव्यसाचिनि ।
बभूवुः कौरवेयास्ते दुःखशोकपरायणाः ॥

meaning.en: When the Pandava Savyasachi had left Kamyaka, my dear, the Kauravas there were given over to sorrow and grief.

verses.text:
आक्षिप्तसूत्रा मणयश्छिन्नपक्षा इव द्विजाः ।
अप्रीतमनसः सर्वे बभूवुरथ पाण्डवाः ॥

meaning.en: Like jewels whose string has been snapped, or birds with clipped wings, all the Pandavas were downhearted.

verses.text:
वनं च तदभूत्तेन हीनमक्लिष्टकर्मणा ।
कुबेरेण यथा हीनं वनं चैत्ररथं तथा ॥

meaning.en: That forest, lacking the man of untiring deeds, was like the garden Chaitraratha when it lacks Kubera.

verses.text:
तमृते पुरुषव्याघ्रं पाण्डवा जनमेजय ।
मुदमप्राप्नुवन्तो वै काम्यके न्यवसंस्तदा ॥

meaning.en: Without that tiger among men, the Pandavas found no joy, Janamejaya, and lived on at Kamyaka.

verses.text:
ब्राह्मणार्थे पराक्रान्ताः शुद्धैर्बाणैर्महारथाः ।
निघ्नन्तो भरतश्रेष्ठ मेध्यान्बहुविधान्मृगान् ॥

meaning.en: Those great warriors, O best of the Bharatas, strove for the brahmins' sake and with clean arrows killed many kinds of animals fit for offering.

verses.text:
नित्यं हि पुरुषव्याघ्रा वन्याहारमरिंदमाः ।
विप्रसृत्य समाहृत्य ब्राह्मणेभ्यो न्यवेदयन् ॥

meaning.en: Every day, those tigers among men, subduers of foes, gathered forest food and spread out to collect it, and gave it to the brahmins.

verses.text:
एवं ते न्यवसंस्तत्र सोत्कण्ठाः पुरुषर्षभाः ।
अहृष्टमनसः सर्वे गते राजन्धनंजये ॥

meaning.en: So they lived there, O king, those best of men, full of longing and joyless, now that Dhananjaya was gone.

verses.text:
अथ विप्रोषितं वीरं पाञ्चाली मध्यमं पतिम् ।
स्मरन्ती पाण्डवश्रेष्ठमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥

meaning.en: Then Panchali, remembering her absent hero, her middle husband, the best of the Pandavas, said this.

verses.text:
योऽर्जुनेनार्जुनस्तुल्यो द्विबाहुर्बहुबाहुना ।
तमृते पाण्डवश्रेष्ठं वनं न प्रतिभाति मे ।
शून्यामिव च पश्यामि तत्र तत्र महीमिमाम् ॥

meaning.en: Arjuna was the equal of the many-armed Kartavirya Arjuna, though he had two arms. Without that best of the Pandavas, the forest does not please me. Everywhere I look, this earth seems empty.

verses.text:
बह्वाश्चर्यमिदं चापि वनं कुसुमितद्रुमम् ।
न तथा रमणीयं मे तमृते सव्यसाचिनम् ॥

meaning.en: This forest, full of wonders and flowering trees, is no longer so lovely to me without Savyasachi.

verses.text:
नीलाम्बुदसमप्रख्यं मत्तमातङ्गविक्रमम् ।
तमृते पुण्डरीकाक्षं काम्यकं नातिभाति मे ॥

meaning.en: Without the lotus-eyed hero who is like a dark rain cloud and has the gait of a rutting elephant, Kamyaka does not shine for me.

verses.text:
यस्य स्म धनुषो घोषः श्रूयतेऽशनिनिस्वनः ।
न लभे शर्म तं राजन्स्मरन्ती सव्यसाचिनम् ॥

meaning.en: I find no peace, O king, remembering Savyasachi, whose bow's twang was heard like thunder.

verses.text:
तथा लालप्यमानां तां निशम्य परवीरहा ।
भीमसेनो महाराज द्रौपदीमिदमब्रवीत् ॥

meaning.en: Hearing her lament thus, Bhimasena, slayer of enemy heroes, said this to Draupadi, O great king.

verses.text:
मनःप्रीतिकरं भद्रे यद्ब्रवीषि सुमध्यमे ।
तन्मे प्रीणाति हृदयममृतप्राशनोपमम् ॥

meaning.en: Slender-waisted lady, what you say is pleasing and delights my mind; it gladdens my heart like a drink of nectar.

verses.text:
यस्य दीर्घौ समौ पीनौ भुजौ परिघसंनिभौ ।
मौर्वीकृतकिणौ वृत्तौ खड्गायुधगदाधरौ ॥

meaning.en: His long, even, sturdy arms are like iron bars, rounded, bearing the scars of the bowstring, and holding sword, weapon and mace.

verses.text:
निष्काङ्गदकृतापीडौ पञ्चशीर्षाविवोरगौ ।
तमृते पुरुषव्याघ्रं नष्टसूर्यमिदं वनम् ॥

meaning.en: Adorned with gold coins and armlets, they are like five-headed serpents. Without that tiger among men, this forest is like a world without a sun.

verses.text:
यमाश्रित्य महाबाहुं पाञ्चालाः कुरवस्तथा ।
सुराणामपि यत्तानां पृतनासु न बिभ्यति ॥

meaning.en: Relying on that mighty-armed one, the Panchalas and the Kurus do not fear even armies of gods, though they strive.

verses.text:
यस्य बाहू समाश्रित्य वयं सर्वे महात्मनः ।
मन्यामहे जितानाजौ परान्प्राप्तां च मेदिनीम् ॥

meaning.en: Relying on that great soul's arms, we all consider our enemies as good as conquered in battle and the earth as already won.

verses.text:
तमृते फल्गुनं वीरं न लभे काम्यके धृतिम् ।
शून्यामिव च पश्यामि तत्र तत्र महीमिमाम् ॥

meaning.en: Without the hero Phalguna I find no comfort at Kamyaka, and everywhere I look, this earth seems empty.

verses.text: नकुल उवाच

meaning.en: Nakula said:

verses.text:
य उदीचीं दिशं गत्वा जित्वा युधि महाबलान् ।
गन्धर्वमुख्याञ्शतशो हयाँल्लेभे स वासविः ॥

meaning.en: He who went to the northern region and defeated mighty fighters in battle, and won hundreds of the finest Gandharva horses, that son of Indra,

verses.text:
राजंस्तित्तिरिकल्माषाञ्श्रीमाननिलरंहसः ।
प्रादाद्भ्रात्रे प्रियः प्रेम्णा राजसूये महाक्रतौ ॥

meaning.en: O king, the glorious Arjuna lovingly gave to his brother at the great Rajasuya sacrifice horses of dappled partridge colour, swift as the wind.

verses.text:
तमृते भीमधन्वानं भीमादवरजं वने ।
कामये काम्यके वासं नेदानीममरोपमम् ॥

meaning.en: Without that godlike one of fearful bow, who is Bhima's younger brother, I do not now wish to live in Kamyaka forest.

verses.text: सहदेव उवाच

meaning.en: Sahadeva said:

verses.text:
यो धनानि च कन्याश्च युधि जित्वा महारथान् ।
आजहार पुरा राज्ञे राजसूये महाक्रतौ ॥

meaning.en: He who defeated great warriors in battle and brought wealth and maidens for the king at the great Rajasuya sacrifice,

verses.text:
यः समेतान्मृधे जित्वा यादवानमितद्युतिः ।
सुभद्रामाजहारैको वासुदेवस्य संमते ॥

meaning.en: he who, alone and of immeasurable splendour, defeated the assembled Yadavas in battle and carried off Subhadra with Vasudeva's approval,

verses.text:
तस्य जिष्णोर्बृसीं दृष्ट्वा शून्यामुपनिवेशने ।
हृदयं मे महाराज न शाम्यति कदाचन ॥

meaning.en: seeing that victor Jishnu's seat empty in our dwelling, my heart, great king, finds no peace at all.

verses.text:
वनादस्माद्विवासं तु रोचयेऽहमरिंदम ।
न हि नस्तमृते वीरं रमणीयमिदं वनम् ॥

meaning.en: I wish, subduer of foes, that we leave this forest and live elsewhere, for without that hero this forest is not pleasant to us.
